clue.text: Prepares last portions of chips and fish with mushy peas

indicators.note: the last portion of each of 'chips' and 'fish' is its final letter
mushy peas have lost their shape, so the letters of PEAS are mashed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone serving up the tail end of a fish supper with mushy peas on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prepares' looks like the start of a cooking instruction, but it is the definition: to shape something is to prepare it. Mushy peas are a British chip-shop side of mashed marrowfat peas.
explanation.definitionFit: To shape a thing is to form or prepare it, as in shaping dough.

clue.text: Lethal venom bottles split into two

indicators.note: the phrase 'Lethal venom' holds the answer inside it the way a bottle holds poison

explanation.surface: A poisoner's bottle of deadly venom, carefully divided in two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottles' reads as a noun, the poison's containers, but it is a verb: the words contain the answer across the gap between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To halve something is to split it into two equal parts.

clue.text: Spray, tip or pour mixture

indicators.note: to spray letters is to scatter them, so they land in a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions for handling a liquid: spray it, tip it or pour it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spray' sits at the front looking like a definition, and potpourri even smells like something sprayed; it is the anagram signal, and 'mixture' at the end defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A potpourri is a mixture, originally of dried petals and spices, and by extension any medley.

clue.text: Tatty, blingy daughters take wife's place

parts.note: d = daughter, twice for the plural
w = wife; this is the letter that goes out

explanation.surface: A family drama: flashy daughters muscling in on their mother's role.
explanation.walkthrough: SHOWY loses its W and gains DD in the same spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoddy and tatty both mean cheap and poorly made.

clue.text: Help politician to conceal British tale of woe

indicators.note: to conceal something is to hide it within, so the letters of 'Help' wrap round those of 'British'

explanation.surface: A politician asked to help cover up something British, which sounds like a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Politician' sits in the middle of the clue, but its letters go last, after the concealing is done. A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A sob story is a tale of woe, usually told to win sympathy.

clue.text: Settled wee kitty moving in and there's no room for any more at this juncture

definitions.text: there's no room for any more at this juncture
definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the point itself

indicators.note: IN moves out of one word and into the other

parts.note: sat = settled, as a bird settles
wee is British slang for urine or urinating
the pot or kitty of pooled money

explanation.surface: A cat settles in its tray, and the room is packed full.
explanation.walkthrough: URINATION gives up its IN, which moves into POT to make POINT: SAT + URATION + POINT. 'Wee kitty' reads as a small cat, but 'wee' is urination and 'kitty' is a pot of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturation point is the stage at which something can absorb no more, where there is no room for any more.

clue.text: Be grateful for entertaining cricket game — it's unreal

parts.note: to bless something is to be grateful for it
ODI = one-day international, a cricket match

explanation.surface: A cricket fan grateful for an entertaining game, then deflated by how unreal it was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entertaining' looks like praise for the match but is the container signal. An ODI is a one-day international, a limited-overs cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bodiless has no physical form, so it is unreal in the sense of insubstantial.

clue.text: Can touring artist work out

explanation.surface: A question: can a touring artist manage to get some exercise?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' opens the clue as a question word, but it is the noun TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the gym sense: exercising to get fit, not solving a problem.

clue.text: Reading magazine nurse leaves after cycling here

indicators.note: the letters of HERE go round, HE moving from front to back
'after' in its sense of 'following in sequence' puts the magazine's letters behind the cycled 'here'

parts.note: HERE with HE cycled to the end
a magazine is a store of weapons
EN = Enrolled Nurse; these letters go

explanation.surface: A reader with a magazine, and a nurse heading off after a bike ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Magazine' suggests reading matter, but it is the weapons store ARSENAL. 'Cycling' looks like the nurse's exercise and is the instruction to rotate HERE.
explanation.definitionFit: A reading of a play, where the cast reads through the script, is a kind of rehearsal.

clue.text: Maybe pancake with essentially watery filling is uninspired

indicators.note: a pancake filling goes inside, so the watery middle is stuffed into the food

parts.note: a pancake is an example of flat food
the middle two letters of watery

explanation.surface: A limp pancake with a soggy middle, served by a cook short of ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' marks the pancake as one example of a wider category; the filling goes into the second word of that phrase only.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat-footed means clumsy and lacking flair, so uninspired.

clue.text: Teacher's anguish

indicators.note: 's stands for 'has': teacher has the answer inside it

explanation.walkthrough: The two-word clue reads as a teacher's distress; the 's does the work of 'has', so the word teacher holds ACHE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a lasting pain, of body or of mind, so anguish.

clue.text: Book again — including a little champagne flute

indicators.note: a booking that includes an extra takes it in, so the champagne letter sits inside 'book again'
a little of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Rebooking a table, with a glass of fizz on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champagne flute' reads as one thing, a glass; the break falls between them, and 'flute' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A recorder is a simple wooden or plastic flute blown from the end.

clue.text: Win gold for coach

parts.note: to land a prize is to win it
Au, the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: An athlete winning a gold medal and dedicating it to their coach.
explanation.walkthrough: The coach here is not a trainer but a horse-drawn vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with a folding top, a type of coach.

clue.text: Consume sport

definitions.meaning: consume in the sense of use up or erode, as water erodes stone
sport as a verb: to have on show, as you sport a hat

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport' looks like a noun, but it is the verb, to show off by wearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Wear means use up by use, as in wear down; and to sport clothes is to wear them.

clue.text: Leader let independent radio broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A leader allowing an independent radio station to go on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' looks like a person, but in British newspapers a leader is the editorial column.
explanation.definitionFit: A leader, or leading article, is a newspaper's editorial.

clue.text: Cassette re-established legal precedent

indicators.note: the letters are set up again in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A cassette tape used to establish a legal point, as recorded evidence might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Re-established' sits between two legal-sounding halves and reads as part of the law, but it only tells you to rearrange CASSETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A test case is a lawsuit whose ruling sets a precedent for others.

clue.text: Judge on wretched TV show

parts.note: to count someone lucky is to judge them so

explanation.surface: A critic calling a television programme wretched.
explanation.walkthrough: Countdown is a long-running British TV word-and-numbers quiz. In a down clue 'on' means placed below, so wretched follows judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Countdown is a British television game show.

clue.text: Scatters seeds containing nitrogen with garden implement — it spreads the load on soft ground

definitions.text: it spreads the load on soft ground

indicators.note: 'containing' in its plain sense of holding within: the seed-scattering word holds the nitrogen symbol

parts.note: to sow is to scatter seed

explanation.surface: A gardener sowing seed, adding nitrogen fertiliser and working the soft soil with a hoe.
explanation.walkthrough: The garden picture makes 'soft ground' look like a flowerbed; the definition means snow.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowshoe spreads the wearer's weight over a wide frame so they do not sink into soft snow.

clue.text: Good nutrient halved in Dr Pepper

indicators.note: 'in' read literally: the halved nutrient is placed in the doctor

explanation.surface: A health claim for the soft drink Dr Pepper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dr Pepper' reads as the brand name; it splits, with Dr the MO and Pepper the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by genus: the pimiento is one variety of sweet red pepper, the kind stuffed into olives.

clue.text: Regularly ignored fungal yeast's beginning to be unsightly

indicators.note: every other letter of fungal is dropped
a word's beginning is its first letter

explanation.surface: A fungal yeast infection left untreated turns unsightly.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters dropped are F, N and A, the odd ones, so the survivors are U, G, L.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugly means unpleasant to look at, unsightly.

clue.text: Emphasise trouble

definitions.meaning: to stress or make much of a point
a verb: to give someone bother, as a bad knee or a naughty child does

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are verbs: 'trouble' is to cause trouble, as a child or an old injury plays up.
explanation.definitionFit: Play up means both to emphasise something and, in British use, to misbehave or cause trouble.

clue.text: Young horse scratching a short tail

explanation.surface: A young horse scratching at its stubby tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short tail' reads as a horse's docked tail; 'short' is LOW and 'tail' is the verb, to follow someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the detective sense: shadowing someone without their knowledge.

clue.text: Crease navy sheets

parts.note: a crease is a line, as on a face

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a crumpled set of dark-blue sheets; 'navy' is the abbreviation N, not a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Bed linen is the collective word for sheets and pillowcases.

clue.text: Friend might — in extremis — greet naked dates found here?

indicators.note: Latin for 'at the extremes': only the end letters of 'might' are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of might

indicators.note: stripped of its outer layer, greet keeps only its middle letters

explanation.surface: A friend meeting naked dates, which sounds like a racy evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dates' look romantic, but here they are the fruit, and the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The date palm is where dates grow, so a palm tree is where dates are found.

clue.text: Join stuck-up priest in bed every now and then

indicators.note: in a down clue, sticking up means reading from bottom to top
only every other letter of 'priest in bed' is taken

explanation.surface: An invitation to join a snooty priest in bed now and again, which is scandalous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuck-up' reads as snobbish, describing the priest; in a down clue it means reversed upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: you join a race or competition by putting your name down for it.

clue.text: Almost destroy new oven

indicators.note: KILL stops one letter short

explanation.surface: Nearly wrecking a brand-new oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New oven' reads as one purchase; 'new' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiln is an oven for firing pottery or bricks.

clue.text: Snooty one in popular comedy ultimately putting sex appeal into play …

indicators.note: 'in' read literally: one is placed in the word for popular
comedy ultimately is its last letter
'putting ... into' is an instruction to insert: sex appeal is placed inside the word for play

parts.note: to toy with = to play with
'it' is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A snob starring in a hit comedy that finally puts some sex appeal into the show.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the next, whose 'short play' continues the theatre story. IT for sex appeal dates from Clara Bow, the 1920s 'It girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoity-toity means haughty and superior, so snooty.

clue.text: … short play, good in points and theatre's booming

indicators.note: PLAY is cut short by its last letter
'in' read literally: good is placed in the points

parts.note: N and E, two compass points

explanation.surface: A short play with good moments, and the theatre is booming with success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Booming' reads as thriving box office; it is the definition in its sound sense. The National Theatre is on London's South Bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Plangent means loud and resonant, with a mournful ring, so booming.

clue.text: Liberal Party Housing Spokesperson finally makes room

indicators.note: to house someone is to take them in, so the party gives a home to the spokesperson's last letter
a liberal arrangement is a free one, so the letters are free to move
spokesperson finally is its last letter

explanation.surface: The Liberal Party's housing spokesperson finally finds a room.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make 'Liberal Party Housing Spokesperson' look like one job title; it breaks into indicator, fodder, indicator and source.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantry is a small room for storing food.
